title: Iteration and Array Utilities
learning_outcomes: Explain what iteration and array utilities contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: foreach.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: PHP arrays are ordered maps that can represent lists, keyed records, and nested collections. Keys, missing values, sorting, and transformation order all affect the resulting data. In this lesson, focus on foreach; then compare it with array_walk(). Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use iteration and array utilities when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: PHP arrays are ordered maps that can represent lists, keyed records, and nested collections. Keys, missing values, sorting, and transformation order all affect the resulting data. For iteration and array utilities, begin with foreach. Also distinguish array_walk(); counting elements; extracting keys and values. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
